Before we sign anything: who has reviewed it?

Finance has. Any support is sized to our fiscal space.

The utility has. We can pay for what we buy.

It is in the least-cost plan, with milestones and a sunset date.

Then we can lend against it.

Then we sign, and we publish it.

THE MoU TRAP · EPISODE 7/7
BEFORE YOU SIGN
RED TEAM
What turns an MoU into a trap?
1Signed before either test is applied
2It costs its signatories almost nothing
3The risk bearers are absent at signature
Bring the risk bearers, and their tests,
to the start of the process.
BEFORE ANY POWER MoU IS SIGNED
01Is it in the least-cost plan, or tested against it?
02Does it carry milestones, a sunset date and, where appropriate, a development security?
03Have the utility and the ministry of finance reviewed it?
04Which layer could block it: sponsor, process, system or fiscal?
05Will it be published in the MoU register?
If not, it is not ready to sign.
AN MoU COSTS ALMOST NOTHING TO SIGN.
It can cost a great deal later.
Bring the risk bearers to the start.
